page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The server provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores via multithreading on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB total, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is not bundled locally, necessitating reliance on external cloud block storage. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest throughput consistent with mature Intel Skylake-era hardware. In CPU testing, the instance achieved a single-core Geekbench score of 989.0 and a multi-core score of 3785.0, accompanied by a Passmark CPU score of 6992.04. Vector instructions such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI are supported, aiding workloads like 135M-parameter LLM inference, which reached 454.02 prompt tokens per second and 116.97 generation tokens per second. However, heavier workloads face compute bottlenecks, with 7B LLM generation dropping to 5.21 tokens per second. Memory bandwidth registers at 40.27 GB/sec for uncached reads and 35.09 GB/sec for uncached writes, while Redis SET operations reached 5.55 million operations per second and web serving delivered 5.7 GB/sec throughput.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a compute-focused resource balance, though overall raw performance lags behind newer generational instance families. Because there is zero local storage and baseline network throughput is capped at 2 Gbps, I/O-intensive workloads may encounter latency overheads over attached network disks. The instance operates best as a stable compute platform for standard web services, batch processing, background workers, and CI/CD compilation pipelines where predictable CPU allocation is necessary without requiring top-tier single-thread velocity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio across 4 physical cores with multithreading. It includes no bundled local storage and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, lacking discrete GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks reflect mature CPU execution, scoring 989.0 in Geekbench single-core, 3785.0 in multi-core, and 6992.04 in Passmark CPU tests. Memory read throughput reaches 40.27 GB/sec on large uncached blocks, and Redis throughput tops 5.55 million SET operations per second. The instance is suited for batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed backend microservices, and general compute-oriented tasks that do not demand high single-thread frequencies or high network throughput.
